findings.detail: hook_runtime builds x-codex-turn-metadata from the current TurnMetadataState/McpTurnMetadataContext. StopRequest retains it; executor-scoped dispatcher clones it into the scheduled task; mcp_runner forwards it unchanged in HookMcpCall.metadata. Original CoreHookMcpExecutor replaced the whole map with threadId alone.

Candidate consumes the per-call map, then unconditionally inserts the executor-owned self.thread_id under threadId. Conflicting inbound threadId cannot override this owner routing field. None and empty metadata retain the original threadId-only request.

No shared mutable metadata map is introduced. Dispatcher takes its per-event snapshot before scheduling, and the candidate owns its incoming map. It does not read later mutable turn metadata, change session binding, broaden visibility or use metadata to choose a different MCP binding.

The existing MCP metadata builder removes harness tool inventory and agent/parent/root identifiers and uses its MCP-specific template. The candidate forwards this already-built map; it does not serialize unfiltered response metadata or import configured response-only extras.

Whole-file inverse confirms weak-session upgrade, HeptaGovernance/active-tool-policy rejection, current_binding, prepare_call, input, timeout, error/text result handling and their order are unchanged. Existing environment binding behavior is untouched and is outside this narrow repair.

Original executor_stop_hook_runs_after_attachment checks no call before attach, one after attach, turn_id parity, session/thread/model parity and owner threadId. All source bytes and assertions of that existing integration test remain unchanged; no mirror test added.

original_failure.assertion: arguments.turn_id was a string while _meta[x-codex-turn-metadata].turn_id was Null

scope: Read-only independent code review. No Rust tests run by reviewer; native original strict/full regression remains required. The patch changes metadata forwarding behavior intentionally and does not claim broader MCP security qualification.
